methods.notes: Watches advertise a "Pebble ..." name and pair as a standard BLE (or Bluetooth Classic on older models) device. A client connects over one of the libpebble2 transports.

device.manufacturer: Pebble Technology (defunct 2016; revived via Rebble + Core Devices)
device.name: Pebble Smartwatch (Classic / Time / Pebble 2 / 2025 revival)
device.notes:
Pebble is the original crowdfunded smartwatch line (Classic, Steel, Time, Time Steel/Round, Pebble 2). Pebble Technology shut down in 2016 (IP to Fitbit then Google), but this is the model rescue story: in Dec 2025 Google open-sourced the PebbleOS firmware 100%, Core Devices ships new Pebble-compatible hardware, and the Rebble Foundation runs the web services and appstore. Full local control, no cloud.
APPLICATION LAYER — the "Pebble Protocol": endpoint-addressed packets. Framing is exactly u16 BIG-ENDIAN body length at bytes 0-1 (EXCLUDING the four-byte length/endpoint header), u16 BIG-ENDIAN endpoint at bytes 2-3, then exactly body_length bytes of body. Field types: Uint8/16/32/64, Int*, Boolean, UUID; four string encodings (PascalString, NullTerminated, Fixed, BinaryArray); Union/FixedList/PascalList/Embed/Padding/Optional. Default field endianness is big-endian, configurable per field.
TRANSPORTS: direct Bluetooth serial to a paired watch at 115200 baud; phone-hosted PPoGATT (10000000); Pebble-2 watch-hosted V1 (30000003) and reversed V2 (40000000). Watch-hosted services are declared under services; the phone-hosted forward definition is under protocol_details.pebble_protocol.transports.ppogatt_forward. A WebSocket via the phone app's Developer Connection (port 9000); and QEMU. Pebble supports only one simultaneous connection — disconnect the phone before connecting a computer over serial. No cloud is needed for protocol operation. Generation-specific GATT/battery support and firmware-update transport are not generalized.
Endpoint NUMBER assignments beyond examples should be taken from libpebble2 source per message type.

openness.notes: libpebble2 was an official Pebble library, so much is documented rather than reverse-engineered; the firmware itself was open-sourced by Google in 2025. Rebble runs the appstore/web services; Core Devices ships new compatible hardware.

enter_pairing_mode.indicator: The watch's Bluetooth settings screen reads "Now Discoverable".
enter_pairing_mode.notes: A watch is discoverable during first-run setup and, after that, while its Bluetooth settings screen is open — not all the time. Pairing is started from the phone app, not from the phone's own Bluetooth settings: Pebble's help and Gadgetbridge both warn that pairing the LE side through the OS menu breaks it.

procedures.basis: Pebble's own help articles (Pebble Time settings; iOS pairing), preserved by the Rebble archive, and Gadgetbridge's Pebble pairing guide for Pebble 2 and Core Devices watches.
procedures.name: Open Bluetooth settings on the watch, then accept the prompt

steps.action: On the watch, open Settings, then Bluetooth, and leave the screen open.
Start pairing from the phone or client app and pick the watch from its list.
Accept the phone's pairing prompt, then press the check-mark (Up) button on the watch to confirm.
steps.expect: The watch shows it is connected.

exclusivity.notes: The watch's Bluetooth settings list the devices it has paired with, so it remembers more than one; it serves only one at a time.
exclusivity.recovery: Disconnect or close the phone app (the Pebble/Core app, Rebble or Gadgetbridge) before connecting from a computer; the watch talks to one host at a time. If pairing loops between connecting and negotiating, forget the phone on the watch (Settings, Bluetooth, the phone, Forget) AND forget every Pebble entry on the phone, then pair again from scratch.

pairing.notes: Ordinary Bluetooth pairing, confirmed on the watch: the Pebble Protocol rides a link to an already-paired watch, so pairing is a precondition the host stack and the phone app handle rather than a step a protocol client implements. Older watches (Classic, Steel, Time) hold two pairings with a phone — a Classic one ("Pebble XXXX") and an LE one ("Pebble-LE XXXX") — and both have to be cleared when a pairing goes bad; Pebble 2 and the 2025 Core Devices watches are LE-only. No credential sits above the bond: once paired, the watch answers the protocol. Medium confidence: Pebble's archived help, the PebbleOS developer documentation and Gadgetbridge agree, but this project has not paired one.

unpair.clears: That one phone's pairing; apps, settings and other pairings stay.

procedures.basis: Pebble's iOS pairing help article, preserved by the Rebble archive.
procedures.name: Forget the phone from the watch's Bluetooth settings

steps.action: On the watch, open Settings, then Bluetooth, select the phone and choose Forget.
On the phone, forget the watch in Bluetooth settings — on older watches both the "Pebble" and "Pebble-LE" entries.

credentials.notes: Standard Bluetooth pairing; no application-layer credential. No Wi-Fi on the watch itself.

factory_reset.description:
Two routes with different reach, and the button one is what matters for abandoned hardware: it works on a watch that is frozen, unresponsive or has no working phone app to drive the menu, which after the vendor's shutdown is most of them.
Button combinations differ across the range. Back, Up and Select together covers most models; the Steel is documented as Back and Select held for about ten seconds. Hold until the Pebble logo appears.
factory_reset.effect: Erases everything held on the watch — installed watchapps, settings and local data — and returns it to first-run state, so it must be paired and set up again.

procedures.basis: Pebble's own help documentation, preserved by the Rebble archive.
procedures.name: Factory Reset from the watch's own menu

steps.action: On the watch, open Settings, then System, then Factory Reset.

procedures.basis: Pebble's help documentation and community troubleshooting guides. Combinations differ by model; the Steel is documented separately.
procedures.name: Hard reset from the buttons (frozen or unresponsive watch)

steps.action: Hold Back, Up and Select together until the Pebble logo appears. On the Pebble Steel, hold Back and Select for about ten seconds.
steps.expect: The watch restarts to the Pebble logo.

methods.description: Pair the watch over Bluetooth, then speak the Pebble Protocol over one of the libpebble2 transports (Bluetooth serial to a paired watch, or a WebSocket developer connection on port 9000). Only one connection at a time.

steps.action: Connect via libpebble2 (Bluetooth serial, or the port-9000 WebSocket dev connection) and exchange Pebble Protocol packets.

setup.notes: Standard Bluetooth pairing; no vendor auth key. App installs now come from the Rebble appstore (apps.rePebble.com) and the mobile app can subscribe to multiple appstore feeds, so anyone can host a Pebble-compatible feed. High confidence: official library docs + the 2025 open-source release.

rejoin.notes: Re-pair over Bluetooth; no network membership to change.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The Pebble Protocol framing and libpebble2 transports are from the libpebble2 documentation; the 2025 open-source status from Core Devices / Google announcements.

pebble_protocol.concurrency: One connection at a time — disconnect the phone before connecting a computer over serial.
pebble_protocol.field_types: Uint8/16/32/64, Int*, Boolean, UUID; strings PascalString/NullTerminated/Fixed/BinaryArray; Union/FixedList/PascalList/Embed/Padding/Optional. Big-endian by default, configurable per field.

framing.body_length: u16 big-endian at bytes 0-1; counts body bytes only and excludes the four-byte header

pebble_protocol.ppogatt_packet: One-byte header: sequence number in bits 3-7 and packet type in bits 0-2; data=0, ack=1, ResetRequest=2, ResetComplete=3. Payload then carries the Pebble Protocol stream.

transports.bluetooth_serial: Direct to a paired watch over the OS Bluetooth serial stack at 115200 baud.

ppogatt_forward.directions: Phone is GATT server and watch is GATT client. Watch reads meta, writes data to the phone and starts ResetRequest; phone notifies the watch. This phone-hosted definition is NOT a watch service and is deliberately absent from top-level services.

transports.ppogatt_reversed_v2: Watch-hosted 40000000 service; phone starts ResetRequest; no meta.
transports.ppogatt_watch_v1: Pebble-2 watch-hosted 30000003 service with separate notify/write/meta characteristics.
transports.websocket: Via the phone app's Developer Connection, TCP port 9000 (MessageTargetPhone).

pebble_protocol.unresolved: Generation-specific battery/GATT support and firmware-update transport/signing are not established; do not generalize one watch generation's endpoints.

characteristics.name: V1 Watch Data Write
characteristics.notes: Phone -> watch PPoGATT packets; separate from the notify UUID.

services.name: PPoGATT Watch-Server V1 (Pebble 2)
services.notes: Watch-hosted V1 on Pebble 2. Phone reads meta and subscribes to watch data notifications; phone writes the separate data-write characteristic. UUIDs use the Pebble base.

characteristics.name: V2 Watch Data (notify)
characteristics.notes: Watch -> phone PPoGATT packets, including reset responses and data.

characteristics.name: V2 Watch Data Write
characteristics.notes: Phone -> watch PPoGATT packets; phone sends initial ResetRequest here.

services.name: PPoGATT Reversed V2 Service (watch-hosted)
services.notes: Watch hosts V2 and phone is GATT client. After subscribing, the PHONE sends the first ResetRequest to 40000003; watch replies on 40000001. No meta characteristic exists (40000002 is reserved, not a data endpoint). Do not treat forward phone-hosted PPoGATT as the same GATT service with reversed characteristic numbers.
